Panorra Content Access Consent Modal

1. User Stories

US-001: Access Protected Content as Guest

As a guest user
I want to view Panorra content previews while browsing
So that I can understand the value of the platform before creating an account.

US-002: Continue Exploring Through Authentication

As a guest user
I want to sign up or log in when access is restricted
So that I can view photos, videos, places, creators, and community content.

US-003: Understand Why Login Is Required

As a guest user
I want to see a clear explanation before authentication
So that I understand the benefit of creating an account.

US-004: Exit the Authentication Prompt

As a guest user
I want to close the popup
So that I can continue browsing available public content.

US-005: Avoid Repeated Interruption

As a guest user
I want to avoid seeing the same modal every time I reopen Panorra
So that I can browse public content without unnecessary interruption.

2. Requirement Specification

Wireframe

Functional Requirements

FR-001: Trigger Authentication Modal

The system shall display the authentication consent modal only when an unauthenticated user attempts to access restricted Panorra content or perform a protected action.

Protected actions may include:

  • Opening full post details
  • Viewing a complete photo or video gallery
  • Accessing restricted creator content
  • Saving or bookmarking content
  • Following creators, places, or hashtags
  • Liking or commenting on content
  • Sending messages
  • Creating or uploading content

The modal shall not automatically appear solely because a guest opens the Panorra website.

FR-002: Modal Content

The popup shall contain:

  • Panorra branding
  • User or account illustration
  • Clear headline
  • Supporting description
  • Terms of Use link
  • Privacy Policy link
  • Sign Up primary action
  • Log In secondary action
  • Close button

FR-003: Sign Up Action

When the user selects Sign up:

  • The user shall be redirected to the registration flow.
  • The current content or protected-action context shall be preserved.
  • After successful registration, the user shall return to the previous content or continue the original action.

FR-004: Log In Action

When the user selects Log in:

  • The user shall be redirected to the authentication flow.
  • The current content or protected-action context shall be preserved.
  • After successful authentication, the user shall return to the previous content or continue the original action.

FR-005: Close Action

When the user selects the close button:

  • The modal shall disappear.
  • The user shall remain on the current page.
  • No account creation shall be forced.
  • The protected action shall not be completed.
  • The modal dismissal timestamp shall be stored locally.

FR-006: Modal Dismissal Persistence

The system shall store the most recent modal dismissal time using a cookie or localStorage.

Recommended key:

panorra_auth_modal_dismissed_at

The stored value should be an ISO 8601 timestamp or Unix timestamp.

FR-007: Cooldown Period

The system should use a configurable cooldown period, with a recommended default of 24 hours.

During the cooldown period:

  • The modal shall not appear automatically.
  • Public content shall remain browsable.
  • A new protected action may display the modal again when authentication is required to complete that action.

FR-008: Authenticated User Exclusion

The modal shall never be displayed to a user with a valid authenticated session.

FR-009: Browser Storage Limitations

The modal may appear again when:

  • The cooldown period has expired
  • Browser cookies or local storage have been cleared
  • The user opens Panorra in private or incognito mode
  • The user uses another browser or device
  • The authentication session has expired and a protected action is attempted

FR-010: Background Interaction

While the modal is open:

  • The page background shall be dimmed.
  • Background interaction shall be disabled.
  • Keyboard focus shall remain inside the modal.
  • Closing or completing authentication shall restore page interaction.

3. Acceptance Criteria

Modal Display

Given a guest user is browsing public Panorra content
When the user has not requested a protected action
Then the modal is not displayed automatically.

Given a guest user attempts a protected action
When authentication is required
Then the modal appears.

When the modal appears:

  • The background is visually dimmed.
  • The modal is centered and clearly visible.
  • Background interaction is disabled.
  • The protected action is paused.

Content Clarity

The modal must:

  • Explain why authentication is required.
  • Explain the benefit of joining Panorra.
  • Provide clear Sign Up and Log In actions.
  • Provide access to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Interaction

The user can:

  • Close the modal.
  • Start registration.
  • Start login.
  • Open the Terms of Use.
  • Open the Privacy Policy.
  • Navigate all interactive elements using a keyboard.

Dismissal and Reopening

Given a guest closes the modal
When the guest closes and reopens the browser tab within the cooldown period
Then the modal shall not automatically appear on page load.

Given a guest previously closed the modal
When the guest attempts another protected action
Then the system may display the modal again because authentication is required for that action.

Given the cooldown period has expired
When the guest attempts a protected action
Then the modal shall be eligible to appear.

Authentication Completion

Given the user signs up or logs in successfully
Then:

  • The modal closes.
  • The authenticated session is established.
  • The user returns to the previous content.
  • The original protected action resumes where technically possible.

Responsive Behavior

Desktop:

  • The modal appears as a centered overlay.
  • The background remains visible but inactive.

Mobile:

  • The modal adapts to the viewport.
  • Primary and secondary actions remain visible.
  • The modal may use a full-screen dialog or bottom-sheet presentation.

Accessibility

The modal shall:

  • Use role="dialog" and aria-modal="true".
  • Provide an accessible dialog title and description.
  • Move keyboard focus to the modal when opened.
  • Trap focus inside the modal while open.
  • Return focus to the triggering element when closed.
  • Support closing with the Escape key unless the action legally requires explicit consent.
  • Provide sufficient text and control contrast.
  • Include accessible labels for all icon-only controls.

4. Expected Outcome

User Experience Outcome

Users can explore public Panorra content without being interrupted immediately, while clearly understanding why authentication is required for protected actions.

Business Outcome

The feature is expected to increase:

  • User registration conversion
  • Returning authenticated users
  • Community engagement
  • Content interaction
  • Completion of protected actions

Product Outcome

Panorra achieves:

  • A consistent authentication experience
  • Clear permission handling
  • Reduced guest-user friction
  • Better transition from discovery to community participation
  • Measurable modal conversion and dismissal behavior

5. User Flow

Guest opens Panorra
        |
        v
Browse public content
        |
        v
Attempts protected action?
   |                |
   | No             | Yes
   v                v
Continue        Check authentication
browsing             |
                     v
                 Logged in?
                |          |
                | Yes      | No
                v          v
          Complete action  Show consent modal
                               |
                 +-------------+-------------+
                 |             |             |
                 v             v             v
              Sign Up        Log In         Close
                 |             |             |
                 v             v             v
          Registration   Authentication   Save dismissal
                 |             |          timestamp
                 +-------> Return to <---------+
                           previous content

6. Modal Behavior and Persistence

6.1 Default Display Behavior

The modal is action-triggered. It shall not display every time a guest opens Panorra.

A guest may access:

  • Public landing pages
  • Public search results
  • Public previews
  • Limited post previews
  • Public place previews
  • Public creator previews

Authentication is requested only when required to continue an action or access protected content.

6.2 Page Load Behavior

On page load, the application shall:

  1. Check whether the user has an active authenticated session.
  2. If authenticated, never display the guest authentication modal.
  3. If unauthenticated, allow access to public content.
  4. Read the stored dismissal timestamp when available.
  5. Wait for a protected action before displaying the modal.

6.3 Protected-Action Behavior

When a guest attempts a protected action:

IF the user is authenticated
    Complete the action
ELSE
    Preserve the requested action and current URL
    Display the authentication modal

The modal may appear even within the dismissal cooldown when the selected action cannot be completed without authentication. The cooldown prevents unsolicited display; it does not bypass authentication requirements.

6.4 Close and Reopen Behavior

When the guest closes the modal:

  • Store the dismissal timestamp.
  • Keep the guest on the current page.
  • Do not complete the protected action.
  • Do not automatically reopen the modal during ordinary browsing.

When the guest closes the browser tab and later reopens Panorra:

  • The modal shall not automatically display if the dismissal record remains valid.
  • The guest may continue browsing public content.
  • The modal may display again when another protected action is attempted.

6.5 Recommended Decision Logic

IF authenticated_session_is_valid
    DO NOT show modal

ELSE IF protected_action_requested
    SHOW modal

ELSE IF dismissal_timestamp exists
        AND current_time - dismissal_timestamp < cooldown_period
    DO NOT show modal automatically

ELSE
    DO NOT show modal automatically
    Wait for a protected action

6.6 State Data

Recommended client-side state:

{
  "panorra_auth_modal_dismissed_at": "2026-07-18T09:30:00.000Z",
  "panorra_pending_action": {
    "type": "save_post",
    "resourceId": "post_123",
    "returnUrl": "/post/post_123"
  }
}

Sensitive authentication data shall not be stored in this client-side modal state.

6.7 Analytics Events

Recommended analytics events:

  • auth_modal_viewed
  • auth_modal_closed
  • auth_modal_signup_clicked
  • auth_modal_login_clicked
  • auth_modal_terms_clicked
  • auth_modal_privacy_clicked
  • auth_modal_auth_completed
  • auth_modal_pending_action_completed

Each event should include non-sensitive context such as:

  • Triggering action
  • Content type
  • Entry page
  • Device type
  • Modal variant
  • Authentication outcome

Panorra Help Center

Product Specification and Acceptance Criteria

Document status: Draft 1.0
Product: Panorra 360
Page: Help Center
Primary platform: Responsive web
Audience: Panorra users, prospective users, parents or guardians, and support staff

1. Product Overview

The Panorra Help Center is a self-service support page that helps users find answers, browse support topics, read filtered FAQs, and access key policy and safety resources.

The page must reduce support friction by presenting clear search, structured topic navigation, context-aware FAQs, and direct access to support channels.

2. Product Goals

  1. Help users find relevant support information quickly.
  2. Reduce repetitive support requests.
  3. Organize FAQs by topic and filter them dynamically.
  4. Make policy, privacy, and youth safety resources easy to access.
  5. Maintain a visual style consistent with the Panorra 360 product.
  6. Support mobile, tablet, and desktop layouts.

3. Success Metrics

Metric Target
Search-to-answer success rate At least 70%
Topic-card to FAQ engagement rate At least 35%
FAQ expansion rate At least 25%
Support contact deflection At least 20%
Average time to first useful action Under 10 seconds
Mobile usability score At least 90
Accessibility score At least 90

4. User Stories

Primary Users

  • As a new user, I want to learn how to start using Panorra 360.
  • As a creator, I want help uploading photos and 360 content.
  • As an account holder, I want to manage my profile and account settings.
  • As a user, I want to understand privacy and safety controls.
  • As an explorer, I want help discovering places and connecting with others.
  • As a user with a technical issue, I want troubleshooting guidance.
  • As a parent or guardian, I want access to youth safety information.
  • As a user who cannot find an answer, I want to contact support.

5. Information Architecture

The Help Center page contains the following sections:

  1. Breadcrumb
  2. Page title and introduction
  3. Hero support area
  4. Search field
  5. Popular-topic shortcuts
  6. Browse Help Topics cards
  7. Frequently Asked Questions
  8. Helpful Resources
  9. Support call to action

6. Page Structure

Page illustration

6.1 Breadcrumb

Content:

  • Home icon
  • Help Center

Behavior:

  • Home returns users to the main Panorra homepage or dashboard.
  • Help Center represents the current page and is not clickable.

6.2 Page Header

Title: Help Center
Subtitle: Find answers, get support, and learn how to make the most of Panorra 360.

Requirements:

  • The title must be visually prominent.
  • The subtitle must use clear, concise language.
  • The section must align with the primary content container.

6.3 Hero Support Area

The hero area uses a two-column layout on desktop.

Left Side

  • Branded help illustration
  • Visual style consistent with Panorra gradients
  • Decorative elements must not interfere with readability

Right Side

Heading: How can we help you?
Supporting text: Search our help articles or browse by category to find the support you need.

Includes:

  • Search input
  • Popular-topic buttons

7. Search Specification

7.1 Search Input

Placeholder: Search for help articles...

Functional requirements:

  • Search must accept keywords and short phrases.
  • Results must match FAQ titles, FAQ content, topic names, and resource labels.
  • Search must be case-insensitive.
  • Search must trim leading and trailing spaces.
  • Search must return partial matches.
  • Search must show an empty state when no result is found.
  • Pressing Enter must submit the query.
  • Search results may appear inline or on a dedicated results page.

7.2 Search States

  • Default
  • Focus
  • Typing
  • Loading
  • Results found
  • No results
  • Error

7.3 Search Empty State

Suggested message:
No matching help articles found. Try another keyword or contact support.

8. Popular Topics

Popular-topic shortcuts appear below the search field.

Required items

  1. Getting Started
  2. Uploading Content
  3. Privacy & Safety
  4. Troubleshooting

Behavior

  • Selecting a shortcut scrolls to the FAQ section.
  • The selected topic becomes active.
  • The FAQ list filters to the selected topic.
  • The selected topic state remains visible.

9. Browse Help Topics

The topic area displays six cards.

9.1 Topic Cards

1. Getting Started

Description: New to Panorra 360? Learn the basics and get started quickly.

2. Uploading Content

Description: Learn how to upload photos, videos, and create 360 content.

3. Account & Profile

Description: Manage your account settings, profile, and privacy preferences.

4. Privacy & Safety

Description: Find out how Panorra keeps users safe and protects personal information.

5. Explore & Connect

Description: Discover places, connect with people, and build your community.

6. Troubleshooting

Description: Get help with common technical issues and platform problems.

9.2 Card Behavior

When a user selects a topic card:

  1. The selected card receives an active border or highlight.
  2. A selected-state icon appears.
  3. The FAQ section updates immediately.
  4. The FAQ section heading shows the active topic.
  5. The page scrolls smoothly to the FAQ section when needed.
  6. Only FAQs assigned to the selected topic are displayed.
  7. Selecting the active card again keeps the topic active.

9.3 Default State

  • Default topic: All Topics
  • All relevant FAQs appear before the user chooses a category.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

10.1 Section Header

Title: Frequently Asked Questions

The section must show either:

  • A topic filter row, or
  • A status label such as Showing FAQs for Privacy & Safety

10.2 Topic Filters

Required filters:

  • All Topics
  • Getting Started
  • Uploading Content
  • Account & Profile
  • Privacy & Safety
  • Explore & Connect
  • Troubleshooting

A More menu may be used on smaller screens or when horizontal space is limited.

10.3 FAQ Accordion

Each FAQ item includes:

  • Question
  • Expand or collapse icon
  • Answer content

10.4 Accordion Behavior

  • Selecting a closed item expands it.
  • Selecting an open item collapses it.
  • At least one item may remain open.
  • The design may allow one or multiple open items.
  • Keyboard users must be able to open and close each item.
  • Expanded state must use aria-expanded="true".

10.5 Example FAQ Content

All Topics

  • What is Panorra 360?
  • How do I create my account on Panorra 360?
  • How do I upload 360 photos or videos?
  • Can I edit my 360 content after uploading?
  • How can I control my privacy on Panorra 360?

Privacy & Safety

  • How does Panorra 360 protect my personal information?
  • Who can see my uploaded content?
  • How do I report inappropriate content or behavior?
  • Can I control who contacts me on Panorra 360?
  • How do I delete my account and data?
  • What are Panorra 360's community guidelines?

11. Helpful Resources

The Helpful Resources section must contain four items.

11.1 Required Resource Items

  1. About Panorra
    Learn more about the Panorra mission, platform, and community.

  2. Terms of Service
    Read the rules, terms, and conditions for using Panorra.

  3. Privacy Policy
    Understand how Panorra collects, uses, stores, and protects data.

  4. Youth Safety
    Access safety guidance and resources for young users, parents, and guardians.

11.2 Resource Item Behavior

  • Each item must be clickable.
  • Each item must include an icon, title, description, and directional indicator.
  • Internal pages open in the same browser tab.
  • External resources may open in a new tab.
  • Link destinations must be configurable through the CMS or application settings.

11.3 Content Correction

Use Privacy Policy, not Privacy Police.

12. Support Call to Action

Heading

Still need help?

Supporting text

Cannot find what you are looking for? Contact our support team.

Primary Action

Label: Contact Support

Optional Secondary Action

Label: Live Chat

Behavior

  • Contact Support opens a support form, email workflow, or ticketing page.
  • Live Chat opens the chat interface when agents are available.
  • When live chat is unavailable, show support hours or an offline message form.

13. Visual Design Criteria

13.1 Style

  • Clean and modern interface
  • White primary background
  • Light gray borders
  • Rounded cards
  • Soft shadows
  • Panorra gradient accents
  • Bright icons with category-based colors
  • High contrast for headings and interactive text

13.2 Suggested Color Roles

Role Suggested treatment
Primary accent Purple to pink gradient
Secondary accent Blue
Success or safety Green
Warning or troubleshooting Orange or pink
Main text Dark navy or near-black
Secondary text Medium gray
Border Light gray or pale lavender
Surface White or very light pastel

13.3 Typography

  • Sans-serif typeface
  • Clear hierarchy
  • Large page heading
  • Medium section headings
  • Readable body text
  • Minimum body size of 16 px on desktop where practical

14. Responsive Requirements

Desktop

  • Maximum content width between 1200 px and 1440 px
  • Hero uses two columns
  • Six topic cards in one row where space permits
  • FAQ and Helpful Resources may use a two-column layout

Tablet

  • Hero may remain two columns or stack based on available width
  • Topic cards display in two or three columns
  • FAQ and resources may stack

Mobile

  • Single-column layout
  • Search field uses full width
  • Popular topics wrap or become horizontally scrollable
  • Topic cards stack or use a two-column grid
  • FAQ filters become scrollable or collapse into a dropdown
  • Touch targets must be at least 44 x 44 px

15. Accessibility Requirements

  1. Meet WCAG 2.1 AA requirements.
  2. Maintain sufficient text and control contrast.
  3. Support keyboard navigation across all interactive elements.
  4. Show visible focus indicators.
  5. Use semantic headings in logical order.
  6. Provide accessible labels for icons and search controls.
  7. Mark decorative illustrations as ignored by assistive technology.
  8. Use buttons for interactive filters and accordions.
  9. Use links for navigation to resource pages.
  10. Announce filtered FAQ result changes through an ARIA live region.
  11. Do not use color as the only selected-state indicator.

16. Content Management Requirements

The CMS or admin interface must support:

  • Topic creation and editing
  • Topic icon management
  • FAQ creation and editing
  • FAQ-to-topic assignment
  • FAQ ordering
  • Popular-topic selection
  • Resource link management
  • Search keyword metadata
  • Draft and published status
  • Last updated date
  • Localization fields

17. Data Model

Topic

{
  "id": "privacy-safety",
  "name": "Privacy & Safety",
  "slug": "privacy-safety",
  "description": "Find out how Panorra keeps users safe and protects personal information.",
  "icon": "shield",
  "color": "green",
  "isPopular": true,
  "order": 4
}

FAQ

{
  "id": "faq-protect-personal-information",
  "question": "How does Panorra 360 protect my personal information?",
  "answer": "Panorra uses appropriate security controls and privacy practices to protect user data.",
  "topicIds": ["privacy-safety"],
  "keywords": ["privacy", "data", "security", "personal information"],
  "isPublished": true,
  "order": 1
}

Helpful Resource

{
  "id": "youth-safety",
  "title": "Youth Safety",
  "description": "Safety guidance for young users, parents, and guardians.",
  "icon": "heart-shield",
  "url": "/youth-safety",
  "openInNewTab": false,
  "order": 4
}

18. Functional Acceptance Criteria

AC-01: Page Load

Given a user opens the Help Center
When the page finishes loading
Then the breadcrumb, page header, hero, search, topic cards, FAQ section, resources, and support action are visible.

AC-02: Default FAQ State

Given the page has loaded
When no topic has been selected
Then All Topics is active and the FAQ section displays FAQs from multiple categories.

AC-03: Topic Card Filtering

Given the user is viewing the Browse Help Topics section
When the user selects Privacy & Safety
Then the card becomes visually active and the FAQ list displays only Privacy & Safety FAQs.

AC-04: Topic Status

Given a topic is active
When the FAQ section is shown
Then the active topic name appears in the filter state or section status label.

AC-05: FAQ Expansion

Given an FAQ item is collapsed
When the user selects the question
Then the answer expands and the accordion control reflects the open state.

AC-06: FAQ Collapse

Given an FAQ item is expanded
When the user selects the question again
Then the answer collapses.

AC-07: Search Match

Given the user enters privacy
When the search is submitted
Then the page displays matching FAQs and resources related to privacy.

AC-08: Search Empty State

Given the user enters a query with no matches
When the search is submitted
Then the page displays a clear no-results message and a Contact Support option.

AC-09: Popular Topic Shortcut

Given the user selects a popular topic
When the interaction completes
Then the corresponding topic becomes active and the FAQ section is filtered.

AC-10: Helpful Resources

Given the user views Helpful Resources
Then the following items are shown in this order:

  1. About Panorra
  2. Terms of Service
  3. Privacy Policy
  4. Youth Safety

AC-11: Resource Navigation

Given the user selects a resource item
When the link is valid
Then the correct destination opens.

AC-12: Contact Support

Given the user cannot find an answer
When the user selects Contact Support
Then the support form, ticketing flow, or configured support channel opens.

AC-13: Keyboard Navigation

Given the user navigates using a keyboard
When the user presses Tab
Then focus moves through search, topic filters, cards, FAQs, resources, and support actions in a logical order.

AC-14: Mobile Layout

Given the viewport width is 375 px
When the Help Center loads
Then all content fits without horizontal page overflow and all interactive controls remain usable.

AC-15: Loading Failure

Given the FAQ service fails
When the FAQ section cannot load
Then the page displays an error message and a retry action.

19. Non-Functional Criteria

Performance

  • Largest Contentful Paint below 2.5 seconds on a typical 4G connection.
  • Cumulative Layout Shift below 0.1.
  • Interaction to Next Paint below 200 ms where practical.
  • Images must use modern formats and responsive sizing.
  • FAQ data should load efficiently and support caching.

Security

  • Sanitize all CMS-provided content.
  • Validate resource URLs.
  • Do not expose sensitive support or account data.
  • Use secure forms for support submission.
  • Apply rate limiting to public search and support endpoints where required.

SEO

  • Use a unique page title and meta description.
  • Use semantic heading structure.
  • Add FAQ structured data where content and implementation comply with search-engine guidelines.
  • Use descriptive internal links.
  • Ensure the page remains indexable unless product policy states otherwise.

20. Analytics Events

Recommended events:

Event Trigger
help_center_viewed Page loads
help_search_submitted Search submitted
help_search_no_results No search result found
help_topic_selected Topic card or filter selected
help_faq_expanded FAQ opened
help_resource_clicked Helpful resource selected
help_contact_support_clicked Contact Support selected
help_live_chat_clicked Live Chat selected

Recommended event properties:

  • Topic name
  • FAQ ID
  • Search query
  • Result count
  • Resource name
  • Device type
  • User status

21. QA Checklist

  • Breadcrumb links work correctly.
  • Search returns relevant matches.
  • Search handles empty and invalid queries.
  • Popular-topic shortcuts filter FAQs.
  • Each topic card filters FAQs correctly.
  • Selected topic state remains visible.
  • FAQ accordion opens and closes correctly.
  • Helpful Resources contain the four approved items.
  • Privacy Policy spelling is correct.
  • All resource links are valid.
  • Contact Support opens the configured flow.
  • Keyboard navigation works.
  • Focus states are visible.
  • Screen-reader labels are accurate.
  • Mobile layout has no horizontal overflow.
  • Tablet and desktop layouts match design intent.
  • Error and empty states are implemented.
  • Analytics events fire once per action.
  • Performance targets are met.
  • Content is editable through the CMS.

22. Definition of Done

The Help Center is complete when:

  1. All approved sections are implemented.
  2. Search works across FAQs, topics, and resources.
  3. Topic cards filter FAQs immediately.
  4. FAQ accordions work across supported devices.
  5. Helpful Resources show About Panorra, Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and Youth Safety.
  6. Support actions lead to valid support channels.
  7. Accessibility, responsive, performance, and QA criteria pass.
  8. Analytics tracking is verified.
  9. Product, design, content, engineering, and QA stakeholders approve the release.

Functional Criteria & Requirements - Contact Us Page

Purpose

The Contact Us page allows users to reach the Panorra 360 team for questions, feedback, support, or partnership inquiries.

The page is designed as a simple, user-friendly single page with:

  • a contact form,
  • multiple contact methods,
  • quick help access,
  • office location information.

Wireframe

Functional Criteria

1. Page Access

  • Users can access the Contact Us page from the application navigation or footer.
  • The system shall display the Contact Us page within the existing application layout.
  • The page shall maintain consistent header, sidebar, and footer components.

2. Page Header

The system shall display:

  • Page title: Contact Us
  • Short welcoming introduction
  • Breadcrumb navigation

Example:
Home > Contact Us

3. Intro / Hero Section

The system shall display:

  • A friendly introductory message
  • Supporting banner or illustration
  • Short explanation encouraging users to reach out

Example copy:

We’d love to hear from you! Whether you have a question, feedback, or partnership idea, our team is here to help.

4. Contact Form Section

The system shall provide a contact form for users to send messages.

Form Fields

  • Full Name
  • Email Address
  • Subject
  • Message
  • Attachments
  • Send Message button

Form Requirements

  • Users can type and submit an inquiry.
  • Required fields must be clearly indicated.
  • The system should validate the form before submission.
  • The system should show success or error feedback after submission.

5. Attachment Upload Requirement

The contact form shall allow users to upload supporting files.

Attachment Rules

  • Users can upload multiple attachments.
  • Supported attachment types may include:
    • Images
    • PDF files
    • Documents
    • Other common file types
  • The attachment field should clearly explain that multiple files are allowed.
  • The UI should provide a visible upload area or drag-and-drop zone.
  • The system should validate file type and upload limits.
  • The system should show uploaded file names or upload status after selection.

Example helper copy:

Upload one or more files (images, PDF, documents, etc.).
You can attach multiple files.

6. Other Ways to Reach Us Section

The system shall display alternative contact methods.

Information may include:

  • Email address
  • Phone number
  • Office address
  • Social media links

Each method should be clearly labeled and easy to scan.

7. Quick Help Section

The system shall provide a quick help section for self-service support.

Requirements:

  • Display short help message
  • Provide button or link to Help Center / FAQ

Example:

Looking for quick answers? Check out our Help Center for guides and FAQs.

8. Map / Office Location Section

The system shall display office location information.

Requirements:

  • Show office address
  • Show map preview or location card
  • Provide button to open or view the map

Example:

Come say hello! We’re always happy to meet our community and partners in person.

UI Requirements

Layout

  • Single-page layout
  • Clear separation between form, contact details, quick help, and map/location sections
  • Logical top-to-bottom flow

Visual Design

The page should maintain:

  • Minimal, clean design
  • Rounded cards
  • Clear headings
  • Consistent icon style
  • Strong visual hierarchy

Responsive Requirements

The system shall support:

  • Desktop
  • Tablet
  • Mobile devices

Form fields, attachment area, and content cards should stack properly on smaller screens.

Page Structure

Order of content:

  1. Contact Us Header
  2. Intro / Hero Banner
  3. Contact Form
  4. Attachment Upload Area
  5. Other Ways to Reach Us
  6. Quick Help Section
  7. Map / Office Location
  8. Footer Links

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Page should load efficiently.
  • Form interaction should be smooth and easy to use.
  • Attachment upload should provide clear status and validation feedback.
  • Content should be readable and accessible.
  • Typography and spacing should support usability.
  • Administrators should be able to update contact details without redesigning the page.

issues.display_title: Issue #3211: [Setting] Integrate User Account — Delete Account
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

delete-account.webm

🔌 [Setting] Integrate User Account — Delete Account

Wire the Delete Account flow in the new pages-new Settings screen (settings/user-account).

Based on pages-new (settings/user-account/*). Legacy reference: pages-old/settings/user-account/* + pages-old/settings/settings.service.ts.

Context

pages-new/settings/user-account is currently a static shell — no API, no state, no navigation:

  • username is hardcoded ('harun') instead of coming from the user profile.
  • The Continue button does nothing. The component is routed (settings-routes.ts → component: UserAccountComponent inside <router-outlet>), but the action is exposed as output<void>(). The Router cannot bind outputs (withComponentInputBinding() covers inputs only), so continueDelete is dead code.
  • The whole OTP → deactivate → logout flow that exists in pages-old is missing.

🔗 Endpoints (BE — already used by pages-old)

Step Method Endpoint
Request OTP POST {{baseURLGoPost}}/users/otp-delete
Confirm delete POST {{baseURLGoPost}}/users/deactivate — body { "otp": number }
Load username GET users/detail (already used by EditProfileService)

⚠️ Confirm with BE whether the OTP is still returned in the otp-delete response (legacy auto-filled the field from res.data?.OTP) — if so, it must not be auto-filled in the new flow.

Scope

  • Service layer — add user-account.service.ts + user-account.model.ts, matching the sibling convention (edit-profile, block-post, block-users, affiliate-list). Signal-driven state (loading, sendingOtp, error), responses through runDecryption. No HTTP calls inside the component.
  • Replace the dead output() with inject(Router) / service navigation.
  • Bind the real username from the profile source instead of the hardcoded string (do not read localStorage like legacy).
  • OTP step — request OTP, input + validation, resend with countdown, confirm delete.
  • Post-delete — logout, then redirect to the restore page (legacy: /page/restore).
  • Loading / disabled state on the destructive button (zLoading / zDisabled) to prevent double-submit.
  • Standalone + OnPush, signals, typed reactive form, no any, no ngOnInit + manual subscribe.

🧹 Cleanups to include

  • Use zType="destructive" instead of the hardcoded bg-[#E53935] / hover:bg-[#D32F2F] — the token variant already exists in button.variants.ts and is dark-mode aware (the hex is not). This is the only place in the repo that hardcodes it.
  • Replace arbitrary font sizes (text-[16px], text-[13px], text-[14px]) with the Tailwind scale.
  • Add an auth guard to the settings routes and make the route lazy (loadComponent), consistent with affiliate-list.
  • A11y: wrap the panel in <section aria-labelledby>, add aria-describedby on the button pointing at the consequences copy.
  • Fix the copy — sentences start lowercase, "14 day" → "14 days", inconsistent capitalisation.
  • Remove the redundant wrapper <div class="w-full"> and fix the template indentation.

🧪 Test scenario (for QA)

  1. Username — open Settings → User Account → the account name shown is the logged-in user's, not a placeholder.
  2. Continue — click Continue → the OTP/verification step opens (currently nothing happens).
  3. OTP sent — an OTP is delivered to the account email; the field is empty and must be typed manually.
  4. Resend — countdown runs; Resend is blocked until it reaches 0, then works.
  5. Wrong OTP — invalid/expired OTP → clear error message, user stays on the page.
  6. Success — valid OTP → account deactivated, session logged out, redirected to the restore page.
  7. Re-login — logging back in within 14 days reactivates the account.
  8. Double-submit — button is disabled/loading while the request is in flight.
  9. Dark mode — the destructive button and panel render correctly in both themes.

Acceptance: the Delete Account page shows the real username, runs the full OTP → deactivate flow against the BE, logs the user out and redirects on success, handles errors gracefully, and no longer contains hardcoded data or hardcoded colours.

🌐 Integrate Multi Language — all pages-new pages

Make the new flow (pages-new) fully multi-language so every page/component renders translated copy and responds to the language switcher. Today translation coverage is partial — many pages-new screens still have hardcoded English strings.

Based on pages-new. i18n stack: ngx-translate (translate pipe / translate directive + i18n keys in src/assets/i18n/*.json).

Current state

  • 15 locale files exist: src/assets/i18n/ → da, de, en, es, fr, it, jp, nl, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sv, zh.
  • Only part of pages-new uses translate (~56 of ~142 component/html files) — the rest have hardcoded strings.

Scope

  1. Audit every pages-new page/component for hardcoded user-facing text (labels, buttons, placeholders, empty/error states, toasts, aria-labels).
    • Pages: home (map/place/detail-place/search), post detail (profile/tickets/hotspots/social/comment/reply/menus), fullscreen, create (all steps), explore/search discover, profile (+ subroutes), settings (+ subroutes), restore, page states (404/construction/no-connection), legal pages, dialogs (report/embed/share/block/delete), notifications.
  2. Extract each string to an i18n key (reuse existing keys where present; follow the t_* namespacing already in the files) and use the translate pipe/directive.
  3. Add the new keys to ALL 15 locale files (English as source of truth; other languages translated/placeholder as agreed).
  4. Language switcher — wire the picker (the pages-new/menu-icon "open language picker" is currently a TODO) to change the active language via the translate service; persist the choice (e.g. localStorage) and restore on load.
  5. Layout resilience — verify longer translations (de/ru/fr) don't break buttons/labels/truncation; interpolation (counts, dates) works per locale.

Acceptance criteria

  • No hardcoded user-facing strings remain in pages-new (spot-checked across all listed pages).
  • Every new key exists in all 15 locale files (no missing-key t_* leaking to the UI).
  • The language switcher changes copy across the app live, and the selection persists across reload.
  • Toasts, empty/error states, placeholders, and aria-labels are translated too.
  • Layout holds with the longest-language strings; no clipped/overflowing labels.
  • No console warnings for missing translation keys.

🧪 Test scenario (for QA)

  1. Switch language — pick each language → the current page re-renders in that language immediately.
  2. All pages — navigate through every pages-new page in a non-English language → no English leftovers, no raw t_* keys.
  3. Persist — reload → the chosen language is retained.
  4. States — trigger empty/error/toast/placeholder → all translated.
  5. Layout — in a long-word language (German/Russian), buttons/labels/nav don't clip or break.

Acceptance: all pages-new pages fully translatable via ngx-translate; keys present in all 15 locales; switcher works + persists; states/aria translated; layout resilient; no missing-key warnings.

detail-hashtag.webm

Panorra Hashtag Detail Screen

1. Document Overview

This document defines the product specification and acceptance criteria for the Panorra hashtag detail screen. The page combines a filtered content feed with a location-based map.

The updated layout uses:

  • A fixed primary navigation sidebar
  • A content panel that occupies approximately one-third of the available desktop width
  • A map panel that occupies approximately two-thirds of the available desktop width
  • Category-based filter chips
  • A two-column content card grid

2. Product Goal

The hashtag detail screen helps users:

  1. Understand the context and popularity of a hashtag
  2. Browse posts associated with the hashtag
  3. Filter posts by content category
  4. Explore where posts are located
  5. Follow or share the hashtag
  6. Switch between high-level content discovery and geographic exploration

3. Target Users

Primary users

  • Travelers exploring destinations
  • Local users discovering nearby places
  • Creators publishing location-based content
  • Users following specific interests or communities

User needs

  • Quickly identify relevant posts
  • Understand where content was created
  • Filter content without leaving the page
  • Compare visual content and map locations at the same time
  • Follow popular hashtags and return later

4. Desktop Layout

Layout

4.1 Overall structure

The page consists of three main areas:

  1. Primary navigation sidebar
  2. Hashtag content panel
  3. Interactive map panel

4.2 Width allocation

Recommended desktop proportions:

Region Width
Primary navigation sidebar 72 to 88 px
Hashtag content panel 33% of remaining viewport
Map panel 67% of remaining viewport

The content panel must remain usable at common desktop resolutions. The map should receive the larger share of horizontal space.

4.3 Minimum viewport

Recommended minimum desktop viewport:

  • Width: 1280 px
  • Height: 720 px

At narrower breakpoints, the layout may switch to a stacked or tabbed experience.

5. Primary Navigation Sidebar

The left sidebar remains visible while the user scrolls.

Navigation items

  • Panorra logo
  • Home
  • Explore
  • Map
  • Activity
  • Notifications
  • Create
  • Profile

Active state

The Explore item uses a clear active state.

Notification badge

The Notifications item may display an unread count badge.

Acceptance criteria

  • The sidebar remains fixed on desktop.
  • The active navigation item is visually distinct.
  • Every item includes an icon and label.
  • The Create action is visually emphasized.
  • Notification counts remain legible at 100% zoom.

6. Top Header

The top header spans the main application area.

Components

  • Back button
  • Global search field
  • Notifications icon
  • User avatar

Search placeholder

Search posts, bookmarks, users, hashtags...

Acceptance criteria

  • The back button returns the user to the previous screen.
  • The search field supports text input.
  • The search field remains visible at desktop widths.
  • The avatar opens the account menu.
  • The notification icon displays unread state where applicable.

7. Hashtag Header

The hashtag header appears at the top of the content panel.

Required fields

  • Hashtag name
  • Total post count
  • Weekly growth indicator
  • Primary category
  • Short description
  • Follow or Following button
  • Share button
  • Overflow menu

Example content

  • Hashtag: #WisataSubang
  • Post count: 12.4K posts
  • Growth: 28% this week
  • Category: Travel
  • Description: Temukan keindahan wisata alam, kuliner, dan hidden gem di Subang.

Acceptance criteria

  • The hashtag title is the most prominent text in the content panel.
  • Growth values use positive or negative visual treatment.
  • The Follow button updates immediately after interaction.
  • The share action opens the system share flow or copies the hashtag URL.
  • The overflow menu exposes secondary actions.

8. Category Filter Chips

The previous post-type filters are replaced with category filters.

Example categories

  • All
  • Nature
  • Culinary
  • Culture
  • Hidden Gem
  • Adventure
  • More

Behavior

  • Only one primary category is active at a time.
  • Selecting a chip filters the content grid.
  • Selecting All resets the category filter.
  • Selecting More opens additional categories.
  • Filter state should update the URL where supported.

Acceptance criteria

  • The active chip is visually distinct.
  • The content list updates without a full page reload.
  • A loading state appears while filtered results are fetched.
  • An empty state appears when no posts match the selected category.
  • Keyboard users can move through chips using Tab and activate them with Enter or Space.

9. Sorting

A sort control appears above the content grid.

Supported options

  • Top
  • Recent
  • Most Liked
  • Most Commented
  • Nearest

Acceptance criteria

  • The default option is Top.
  • The selected option persists while category filters change.
  • Sorting updates the post grid without reloading the entire page.
  • Nearest only appears when location permission or a valid location is available.

10. Content Grid

10.1 Grid structure

The post feed uses a two-column grid inside the one-third-width content panel.

10.2 Card content

Each card includes:

  • Creator avatar
  • Creator username
  • Place name
  • Relative post time
  • Overflow menu
  • Main image
  • Like count
  • Comment count

Optional fields:

  • Verification badge
  • Bookmark state
  • Post category
  • Sponsored label
  • Media type indicator

10.3 Image ratio

Recommended image ratio:

  • 4:3 or 16:10
  • Consistent across all cards

10.4 Card behavior

  • Clicking the image opens the post detail page.
  • Clicking the creator opens the creator profile.
  • Clicking the location highlights the corresponding map area.
  • Clicking Like updates the count optimistically.
  • Clicking Comment opens the post discussion.
  • Clicking the overflow menu exposes post actions.

Acceptance criteria

  • Exactly two cards appear per row on supported desktop widths.
  • Card widths remain equal.
  • Images use consistent aspect ratios.
  • Text truncates safely when space is limited.
  • Cards preserve alignment even when usernames or place names vary in length.
  • Loading skeletons match the final card dimensions.
  • Infinite scroll or pagination loads more results without shifting the map.

11. Map Panel

The map occupies approximately two-thirds of the available main viewport.

Map content

  • Base map
  • Place labels
  • Individual photo pins
  • Cluster markers
  • Selected cluster state
  • User location marker
  • Zoom controls
  • Recenter control
  • Location button
  • Post-density legend

Example legend

  • Green: 250+ posts
  • Blue: 50+ posts
  • Gray: 10+ posts
  • Outlined blue marker: Your location

Acceptance criteria

  • The map loads independently from the content grid.
  • Cluster markers display the number of grouped posts.
  • Clicking a cluster zooms into that area.
  • Clicking an image pin highlights or filters related content cards.
  • Clicking a content card location highlights the related map marker.
  • The map preserves its zoom and center while category filters update.
  • Zoom controls and keyboard navigation are accessible.
  • The user location marker appears only after permission is granted.

12. Content and Map Synchronization

The content panel and map must remain synchronized.

Interaction rules

  1. Selecting a category updates visible map markers.
  2. Selecting a map cluster updates or highlights matching content.
  3. Hovering a content card highlights its map marker.
  4. Hovering a map marker highlights its content card.
  5. Sorting the content grid does not change the map viewport.
  6. Applying Nearest sorting may recenter the map around the user.

Acceptance criteria

  • The same post ID is used across card and marker data.
  • Highlighted states are visually consistent.
  • Synchronization does not trigger a full page reload.
  • A failed map request does not prevent the content feed from loading.
  • A failed content request does not prevent the base map from loading.

13. Responsive Behavior

Large desktop

  • Sidebar fixed
  • Content panel approximately one-third
  • Map panel approximately two-thirds
  • Two-column post grid

Tablet

Recommended behavior:

  • Sidebar collapses to icons
  • Content and map may use a 45/55 split
  • Grid may remain two columns if card width stays usable

Mobile

Recommended behavior:

  • Bottom navigation replaces desktop sidebar
  • Content and map appear as separate tabs
  • Content grid becomes one column
  • Filter chips become horizontally scrollable
  • Map opens full width

Acceptance criteria

  • No horizontal page overflow occurs.
  • Filter chips remain accessible on narrow screens.
  • Cards remain readable at every supported breakpoint.
  • Core actions remain reachable without precision clicking.

14. Empty, Loading, and Error States

Loading state

  • Hashtag metadata skeleton
  • Filter chip placeholders
  • Post card skeletons
  • Map loading placeholder

Empty state

Message example:

No posts found in this category.

Actions:

  • Clear filters
  • Select another category
  • Explore nearby hashtags

Error state

Message example:

We could not load these posts. Please try again.

Actions:

  • Retry
  • Refresh map
  • Contact support

Acceptance criteria

  • Every asynchronous region has a loading state.
  • Empty states explain what happened.
  • Error states include a recovery action.
  • Map and content errors are handled independently.

15. Accessibility Requirements

  • Meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast requirements.
  • Provide accessible labels for icon-only buttons.
  • Support keyboard navigation across chips, cards, controls, and map actions.
  • Use visible focus indicators.
  • Do not rely on color alone to communicate state.
  • Provide alternative text for post images.
  • Announce filter result counts to screen readers.
  • Ensure map controls have descriptive names.

16. Performance Requirements

  • Initial meaningful content should render within 2.5 seconds on a typical broadband connection.
  • Images should use responsive sizes and lazy loading.
  • Map markers should use clustering for dense regions.
  • Filter changes should return visible feedback within 300 milliseconds.
  • The app should avoid reloading the map library during content updates.
  • Use pagination or incremental loading for large datasets.

17. Analytics Events

Recommended analytics events:

Event Trigger
hashtag_viewed User opens the hashtag page
hashtag_followed User follows the hashtag
hashtag_unfollowed User unfollows the hashtag
category_filter_selected User selects a category chip
sort_changed User changes sorting
post_card_opened User opens a post
map_marker_selected User selects a map marker
map_cluster_selected User selects a cluster
map_recentered User uses recenter control
hashtag_shared User shares the hashtag

Recommended event properties:

  • hashtag ID
  • category ID
  • sort option
  • post ID
  • marker or cluster ID
  • viewport center
  • zoom level
  • user location permission state

18. Data Model

Hashtag object

{
  "id": "hashtag_wisata_subang",
  "name": "WisataSubang",
  "postCount": 12400,
  "weeklyGrowthPercent": 28,
  "primaryCategory": "travel",
  "description": "Temukan keindahan wisata alam, kuliner, dan hidden gem di Subang.",
  "isFollowing": true
}

Category object

{
  "id": "nature",
  "label": "Nature",
  "icon": "mountain",
  "isActive": false
}

Post card object

{
  "id": "post_001",
  "creator": {
    "id": "user_001",
    "username": "Lundara",
    "avatarUrl": "/assets/users/lundara.jpg"
  },
  "location": {
    "name": "Ciater, Subang",
    "latitude": -6.733,
    "longitude": 107.650
  },
  "createdAt": "2026-07-21T08:00:00Z",
  "imageUrl": "/assets/posts/tea-field.jpg",
  "category": "nature",
  "likeCount": 342,
  "commentCount": 18
}

Map cluster object

{
  "id": "cluster_subang_center",
  "latitude": -6.5716,
  "longitude": 107.7587,
  "postCount": 23,
  "densityLevel": "medium"
}

19. Definition of Done

The screen is complete when:

  • The content panel occupies approximately one-third of the main viewport.
  • The map occupies approximately two-thirds of the main viewport.
  • Category chips replace post-type chips.
  • The content feed uses a two-column grid.
  • Filter, sort, follow, share, map, and post interactions work.
  • Card and marker states stay synchronized.
  • Loading, empty, and error states are implemented.
  • Desktop, tablet, and mobile breakpoints are validated.
  • Accessibility checks pass.
  • Analytics events are implemented.
  • Product, design, and engineering stakeholders approve the final behavior.

Demo by developer

Branch: 3203-hashtag-detail-page · Route: /hashtag?tag=%23360photography · Source: src/app/pages/detail-hashtag/

Halaman sudah dibangun penuh dan terintegrasi dengan API produksi. Bagian di bawah mencatat apa yang jalan, apa yang menyimpang dari spec beserta alasannya, dan apa yang masih menunggu dukungan backend.

Struktur komponen

src/app/pages/detail-hashtag/
├── detail-hashtag.component.ts/html      # halaman: state URL-driven, paging, sinkronisasi pane
├── detail-hashtag.facade.ts              # satu-satunya lapisan HTTP; komponen bebas HTTP
├── detail-hashtag.mapper.ts              # payload API → view model
├── detail-hashtag.model.ts               # view model, taksonomi chip, legend, util tag
├── detail-hashtag-api.model.ts           # tipe respons mentah
├── topbar/                               # §6 back + search + notif + avatar
├── header/                               # §7 nama hashtag, jumlah post, follow, share, overflow
├── filters/                              # §8 chip kategori
├── post-grid/                            # §10 grid 2 kolom, skeleton, empty, load-more
│   └── post-card/                        #     kartu media + badge + overflow
└── map/                                  # §11 map pane + density legend

Semua komponen standalone, ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, signal-based (input/output/computed), Tailwind v4. 76 unit test, semuanya lolos.

Integrasi API

Endpoint Dipakai untuk
GET search/hashtag?tag&limit&page Header — nama hashtag + total post asli
GET search/hashtag-post?tag=%23…&limit&page&category Grid post, dengan paging & filter kategori
GET posts/detail?slug Titik pusat map, diambil dari post terbaru hashtag tsb

Post dengan pending: true disaring karena medianya belum siap. Kegagalan posts/detail sengaja ditelan — map jatuh ke default view-nya sendiri, bukan menjatuhkan seluruh header ke error state.

Sudah sesuai spec

§ Item Keterangan
5, 6 Sidebar + top header Route ter-nest di app shell; topbar punya back, search, notif, avatar
7 Nama hashtag, jumlah post, Follow, Share, overflow menu Follow optimistic + revert & toast bila gagal; Share pakai Web Share API dengan fallback clipboard
8 Chip kategori Single-active, All mereset, state tersimpan di URL (?category=), loading + empty state, keyboard Tab/Enter/Space
10 Grid 2 kolom sm:grid-cols-2, rasio gambar konsisten 16/10, skeleton seukuran kartu final, infinite scroll tanpa menggeser map
12 Hover kartu Kartu yang di-hover ditandai (highlightedPostId); ID post yang sama dipakai lintas kartu & data map
13 Responsive Di bawah md kedua pane jadi tab Posts/Map, grid 1 kolom, chip scrollable, tanpa overflow horizontal
14 Loading / empty / error Setiap region async punya state; error map & konten ditangani independen; empty state menawarkan "Clear filters"; error state menawarkan "Retry"
15 Aksesibilitas aria-label untuk semua tombol ikon, focus ring terlihat, target sentuh ≥44px, role="status" aria-live mengumumkan jumlah hasil filter, alt text gambar
16 Performa Gambar loading="lazy" + decoding="async", paging inkremental (8 per halaman), library map tidak di-reload saat filter berubah

Analytics (§17) — 4 dari 10 terpasang

Terpasang: hashtag_viewed, hashtag_followed, hashtag_unfollowed, category_filter_selected, hashtag_shared.

Belum: post_card_opened, map_marker_selected, map_cluster_selected, map_recentered (bergantung pada interaktivitas map, lihat di bawah), dan sort_changed (tidak berlaku, lihat di bawah).

Menyimpang dari spec — keputusan sadar karena keterbatasan API

§ Spec meminta Yang dikirim Alasan
8 Chip: Nature, Culinary, Culture, Hidden Gem, Adventure, More All / Leisure / Real Estate / Business search/hashtag-post hanya menerima category numerik 0–3. Taksonomi di mockup tidak ada di backend, sehingga chip-nya tidak akan memfilter apa pun. Chip More ikut ditiadakan.
7 Weekly growth, primary category, deskripsi pendek Kosong (otomatis disembunyikan) Tidak ada endpoint. Field-nya sudah ada di view model, tinggal diisi begitu API tersedia.
7 Tombol Follow Optimistic, in-memory saja (hanya bertahan selama tab hidup) Tidak ada endpoint follow hashtag. Halaman sudah menangani promise yang gagal dengan revert, jadi tinggal ganti isi setFollowing.
10.2 Kartu: avatar & username kreator, nama tempat, waktu relatif, like, comment Hanya media + badge POTD / tipe media (Album, Video) search/hashtag-post sama sekali tidak mengirim kreator, lokasi, timestamp, maupun counter engagement. Field yang tak bisa diisi dihapus, bukan diisi nol.
4.2 Panel konten 33% / map 67% Panel konten 44% (min 520px, maks 760px) Pada 33% di viewport 1280px, grid 2 kolom membuat kartu terlalu sempit untuk terbaca. Mohon konfirmasi apakah angka spec tetap wajib.

Belum bisa dikerjakan — butuh dukungan backend / infrastruktur

  1. §9 Sorting (Top / Recent / Most Liked / Most Commented / Nearest). Kontrolnya dihapus: search/hashtag-post tidak punya parameter sort, jadi kontrol apa pun tidak akan mengubah hasil. Feed disajikan dalam urutan bawaan API. Butuh: parameter sort di endpoint.

  2. §11 & §12 interaktivitas map. Map pane memakai embed maps.panorra.com (MapsPanorraComponent) di dalam iframe, sehingga dari sisi PWA tidak bisa dikerjakan:

    • photo pin per post, cluster marker beserta jumlahnya, klik cluster untuk zoom
    • klik pin → memfilter / menyorot kartu terkait
    • hover kartu → menyorot marker-nya (saat ini hanya sisi kartu yang bereaksi)
    • kontrol zoom / recenter, marker lokasi pengguna

    Map sekarang hanya di-center ke koordinat post terbaru hashtag. Legend kepadatan (250+/50+/10+) saat ini dekoratif dan belum terhubung ke data mana pun — mohon keputusan apakah disembunyikan dulu atau menunggu data cluster.

    Butuh: endpoint marker/cluster per hashtag + map SDK di dalam PWA (bukan iframe), atau API postMessage dari embed.

  3. Mute & Report hashtag/post. Item menu sudah terpasang dan menampilkan toast "akan segera tersedia"; alurnya tinggal satu baris begitu endpoint mendarat. Butuh: endpoint mute & report.

Ringkasan Definition of Done (§19)

Kriteria Status
Chip kategori menggantikan chip tipe post ✅ (dengan taksonomi API)
Feed 2 kolom ✅
Loading / empty / error state ✅
Breakpoint desktop, tablet, mobile ✅
Pemeriksaan aksesibilitas ✅
Interaksi filter, follow, share, post ✅
Panel konten ~1/3, map ~2/3 ⚠️ 44% / 56% — perlu konfirmasi
Interaksi sort ❌ tidak didukung API
Sinkronisasi state kartu ↔ marker ⚠️ sebagian — sisi kartu saja, map masih iframe
Analytics event ⚠️ 4 dari 10

Mohon masukan pada tiga hal yang butuh keputusan produk: proporsi panel 33/67, legend kepadatan map, dan prioritas endpoint (sort, marker/cluster, follow, field kartu).

issues.display_title: Issue #3204: Update filter image thumbnail in filter to genral illustration filter
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

screen-capture.28.webm

Panorra 360 Editor Product Specification

1. Overview

This document defines the product specification and acceptance criteria for the updated Panorra 360 image editor.

The editor allows users to upload one or more panorama images, preview the selected image, apply a predefined projection filter, remove the active filter by selecting None, and save the edited result.

The updated design removes the separate right-side filter drawer. Filter options now appear directly in the left editor panel.

2. Product Goal

The editor should help users apply panorama projection filters quickly without requiring them to understand technical projection settings.

The interface should:

  • Keep image management and filters in one panel
  • Use general illustrations instead of user-image thumbnails for filter previews
  • Make the active filter clear
  • Allow users to remove a filter by selecting None
  • Preserve a large central preview area
  • Reduce unnecessary navigation and duplicate controls

3. Main Layout

The desktop editor contains three primary regions:

  1. Primary navigation sidebar
  2. Editor control panel
  3. Main panorama preview canvas

Recommended proportions

Region Recommended width
Primary navigation sidebar 72 to 88 px
Editor control panel 340 to 420 px
Main preview canvas Remaining available width

The preview canvas should remain the dominant visual area.

4. Primary Navigation Sidebar

The left navigation sidebar remains fixed.

Navigation items

  • Panorra logo
  • Map
  • Editor
  • Hotspot
  • Audio
  • Notifications
  • Create
  • Profile

Active state

The Editor item must use a clear active state.

Acceptance criteria

  • The sidebar remains visible on desktop.
  • Each item includes an icon and label.
  • The active page is visually distinct.
  • Notification count badges remain readable.
  • The Create action is visually emphasized.

5. Top Header

The global header spans the application width.

Components

  • Panorra 360 wordmark
  • Notifications icon
  • Language selector
  • User avatar

Acceptance criteria

  • The language selector opens available language options.
  • The avatar opens the user menu.
  • The notification icon shows unread state when applicable.
  • The header remains visually separate from the editor workspace.

6. Editor Control Panel

The editor panel appears between the primary navigation and the preview canvas.

Top actions

  • Back button
  • Save button

Behavior

  • Back returns the user to the previous creation step.
  • Save stores the selected image and active filter state.

Acceptance criteria

  • Back and Save remain visible while the panel scrolls where practical.
  • Save is disabled when no image is available.
  • Save displays progress while processing.
  • Save shows success or error feedback after completion.

7. Images List

The Images List section allows users to manage uploaded panorama images.

Components

  • Selected image card
  • Add Image card
  • Optional delete action on uploaded images

Selected image behavior

  • The active image card uses a selected border or highlight.
  • Selecting another image updates the main preview.
  • Each image maintains its own filter state where supported.

Add Image behavior

  • Selecting Add Image opens the file picker.
  • Supported file validation occurs before upload.
  • Upload progress appears inside the card or nearby.

Acceptance criteria

  • At least one image must be selected before filter controls are enabled.
  • Unsupported files display a clear validation message.
  • Uploaded images display a thumbnail.
  • The selected image is always visually identifiable.
  • Removing the selected image automatically selects the next available image.
  • Removing the final image returns the editor to its empty state.

8. Filter Section

The filter controls appear directly below the Images List.

Components

  • Filter section label
  • Filter enable switch
  • Active filter summary row
  • Two-column filter grid

Filter switch behavior

  • Turning the switch off disables all applied filters.
  • Turning the switch on restores the last selected filter where supported.
  • If no filter has been selected, turning it on keeps the image in the None state.

Acceptance criteria

  • The filter grid is disabled when the section switch is off.
  • The preview updates immediately after the switch changes.
  • The switch state is preserved when the user changes images.

9. Active Filter Summary

The active filter summary appears above the filter grid.

Example

Little Planet

Components

  • Filter icon
  • Active filter name
  • Clear action
  • Close or remove icon

Behavior

  • Selecting Clear resets the active filter to None.
  • Selecting the remove icon performs the same reset action.
  • The preview returns to the original panorama projection.

Acceptance criteria

  • The active filter name always matches the selected filter card.
  • Clear actions are disabled when None is active.
  • Resetting the filter does not remove the uploaded image.
  • Resetting the filter does not alter image metadata.
  • The reset action updates the preview without reloading the page.

10. Filter Grid

The filter grid uses exactly two columns.

Filter order

  1. None
  2. Little Planet
  3. Sky Hole
  4. Dome
  5. Half Pipe
  6. Wide Angle

Removed option

Custom Filter is not included in this version.

Card contents

Each filter card includes:

  • General illustrative preview
  • Filter name
  • Selected state indicator

Illustration requirements

The filter illustrations must:

  • Use a consistent visual scene
  • Show the projection difference clearly
  • Avoid using the user’s uploaded image
  • Use Panorra’s pink, purple, and blue visual language
  • Remain legible at small card sizes
  • Avoid excessive visual detail
  • Use a soft 2.5D or simplified 3D style

None card

The None card appears first.

It should use:

  • A neutral icon
  • No projection illustration
  • A label reading None

Selecting it removes any active filter.

Acceptance criteria

  • Exactly two cards appear per row.
  • Card widths remain equal.
  • Only one filter can be active at a time.
  • The selected card uses a strong border and check indicator.
  • Selecting a filter updates the main preview.
  • Selecting None removes the active filter.
  • Keyboard users can navigate and select filter cards.
  • Filter labels remain readable at 100% browser zoom.

11. Filter Definitions

None

Displays the original panorama without a projection filter.

Little Planet

Transforms the panorama into a compact spherical planet-style composition.

Sky Hole

Wraps the panorama around an open central sky area.

Dome

Projects the panorama into a dome-like hemispherical form.

Half Pipe

Curves the scene upward along both sides, creating a U-shaped projection.

Wide Angle

Expands the field of view and emphasizes horizontal spatial coverage.

12. Main Preview Canvas

The main canvas displays the active image with the selected filter.

Components

  • Large panorama preview
  • Fullscreen or fit-to-screen control
  • Zoom out control
  • Zoom in control

Behavior

  • The preview updates when the user selects an image.
  • The preview updates when the user selects a filter.
  • Zoom controls affect only the preview viewport.
  • Filter state remains unchanged when zoom changes.

Acceptance criteria

  • The preview uses the majority of the available workspace.
  • The image remains centered.
  • The preview maintains the correct aspect ratio.
  • Filter changes display loading feedback when processing takes longer than 300 milliseconds.
  • The canvas does not reset zoom unless required by the projection.
  • Fullscreen mode preserves the active filter.

13. Empty State

When no image is uploaded:

  • The main preview shows a neutral placeholder.
  • The filter section is disabled.
  • Save is disabled.
  • The Add Image card remains available.

Empty-state message

Add a panorama image to start editing.

Acceptance criteria

  • The interface clearly explains the next action.
  • Disabled controls remain visible but non-interactive.
  • The user can upload an image without leaving the screen.

14. Loading and Processing States

Image upload

Show:

  • Upload progress
  • File name
  • Cancel action where supported

Filter processing

Show:

  • Preview loading indicator
  • Temporary disabled state for filter cards when required

Save processing

Show:

  • Save progress
  • Success confirmation
  • Retry action after failure

Acceptance criteria

  • Long-running actions always provide feedback.
  • Users cannot accidentally trigger duplicate save requests.
  • Failed processing does not remove the original image.
  • The last successful filter state remains recoverable.

15. Error States

Possible errors

  • Unsupported file format
  • File too large
  • Upload failed
  • Filter processing failed
  • Preview failed to render
  • Save failed
  • Session expired

Error message principles

Messages should:

  • State what failed
  • Explain the likely cause when known
  • Provide a recovery action
  • Avoid technical jargon where possible

Example

We could not apply this filter. Try again or select another filter.

16. Responsive Behavior

Large desktop

  • Fixed sidebar
  • Fixed editor panel
  • Large preview canvas
  • Two-column filter grid

Tablet

  • Sidebar may collapse to icons
  • Editor panel may reduce in width
  • Filter grid remains two columns where cards stay readable

Mobile

Recommended behavior:

  • Bottom navigation replaces the sidebar
  • Editor panel becomes the main screen
  • Preview appears above controls
  • Filter grid remains two columns
  • Save action becomes sticky at the bottom

Acceptance criteria

  • No horizontal page overflow occurs.
  • Filter cards remain readable.
  • Main actions remain reachable.
  • Preview and controls do not overlap.

17. Accessibility Requirements

  • Meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast requirements.
  • Provide visible focus states.
  • Use accessible names for icon-only controls.
  • Ensure the filter cards can be selected using keyboard controls.
  • Do not communicate selected state by color alone.
  • Announce active filter changes to screen readers.
  • Provide text alternatives for filter illustrations.
  • Maintain minimum touch target sizes on mobile.

Suggested filter card labels

  • No filter
  • Apply Little Planet filter
  • Apply Sky Hole filter
  • Apply Dome filter
  • Apply Half Pipe filter
  • Apply Wide Angle filter

18. Analytics Events

Recommended events:

Event Trigger
editor_opened User opens the editor
image_added User uploads an image
image_selected User selects an image
image_removed User deletes an image
filter_enabled User enables filters
filter_disabled User disables filters
filter_selected User selects a filter
filter_cleared User selects None or Clear
preview_zoomed User changes zoom
preview_fullscreen_opened User opens fullscreen
editor_saved Save completes successfully
editor_save_failed Save fails

Recommended properties

  • image ID
  • image count
  • selected filter
  • previous filter
  • processing duration
  • save duration
  • device type
  • viewport size

19. Suggested Data Model

Filter option

{
  "id": "little-planet",
  "name": "Little Planet",
  "illustrationUrl": "/assets/filters/little-planet.png",
  "enabled": true,
  "order": 2
}

None option

{
  "id": "none",
  "name": "None",
  "illustrationUrl": null,
  "enabled": true,
  "order": 1
}

Editor image

{
  "id": "image_001",
  "sourceUrl": "/uploads/panorama-001.jpg",
  "thumbnailUrl": "/uploads/panorama-001-thumb.jpg",
  "selectedFilter": "little-planet",
  "filterEnabled": true,
  "uploadStatus": "complete",
  "processingStatus": "complete"
}

Editor state

{
  "selectedImageId": "image_001",
  "images": [],
  "isSaving": false,
  "hasUnsavedChanges": true
}

20. Acceptance Criteria Summary

The updated editor is complete when:

  • The right-side filter drawer is removed.
  • Filters appear inside the left editor panel.
  • The filter layout uses two columns.
  • None appears as the first filter option.
  • Custom Filter is removed.
  • General illustrations replace user-image filter thumbnails.
  • Only one filter can be selected at a time.
  • Selecting None clears the active filter.
  • The active filter summary updates correctly.
  • Clear actions reset the filter without deleting the image.
  • The main preview updates after every filter selection.
  • Loading, empty, and error states are implemented.
  • Desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts are validated.
  • Accessibility and analytics requirements are met.

21. Definition of Done

The feature is ready for release when:

  • Product approves the filter list and behavior.
  • Design approves the two-column layout and illustrations.
  • Engineering implements filter selection and reset logic.
  • QA validates all filter states.
  • The preview remains stable during filter changes.
  • Save behavior preserves the selected filter.
  • Accessibility checks pass.
  • Analytics events are verified.
  • No custom filter entry appears in the interface.

issues.display_title: Issue #3214: Integrate Prev Next Fullscreen From Profile
issues.main_description_html:
##Demo by developer

screen-capture.29.webm

🔀 Integrate Prev/Next Fullscreen — From Profile

Wire prev/next navigation in the fullscreen viewer when entered from a Profile (gallery/posts), so the user can swipe/arrow through that profile's posts without leaving fullscreen.

Based on pages-new (pages-new/fullscreen/*, pages-new/profile/*). Sibling contexts: Timeline, Search.

Scope

  • When opening /fullscreen/:slug from a profile gallery, carry the ordered list + current index for that profile's posts so the viewer can go prev/next (arrows on desktop, swipe on mobile) and fetch the next page when the list runs out (continue the profile's pagination). Update the URL/slug as the user navigates. Signal-driven; no BehaviorSubject, no any.

🧪 Test scenario (for QA)

  1. Enter — open a post from a profile gallery in fullscreen → prev/next controls available.
  2. Navigate — next/prev moves through the profile's posts in the correct order; slug/URL updates.
  3. Boundaries — first item has no prev; last item loads the next page (or stops cleanly at the end).
  4. Back — leaving fullscreen returns to the profile at the right scroll position.
  5. Types — panorama / multiple / video / embed each render correctly when navigated to; no console errors.

Acceptance: prev/next traverses the profile's post list (with pagination) from fullscreen; slug/URL + boundaries + back-position handled; no any.

##Demo by developer

screen-capture.28.webm

🎨 Update Image Filter Panorama

Update the image filter (little-planet / creative filter) behaviour on the panorama in the new pages-new create flow.

Based on pages-new (create/filter/*, create.component.ts panoramaFilter() / persistFilterOnActiveImage, live app-view-panorama). Related: hotspot guidance in filtered mode (#3175).

Scope

  • Update the filter UI/behaviour on the panorama (filter list/mode + sliders: north angle, zoom, rotation/curvature) so it matches the current design and applies live to the preview.
  • Persist the filter into the per-image state (CreatePanoramaImage.filterValue / isFilter) via computed(), not effect() side-effects; include it in the create/complete payload.
  • Standalone + OnPush; Tailwind 4 / Zard UI tokens (light + dark); no any.

🧪 Test scenario (for QA)

  1. Apply — toggle/adjust the filter → the preview updates live to reflect it.
  2. Controls — north angle / zoom / rotation / curvature (as designed) change the preview correctly.
  3. Reset — clearing the filter returns the preview to the unfiltered image.
  4. Persistence — navigate steps / switch images and back → the filter is retained per image.
  5. Payload — publish → the filter value is included in the completePost payload.
  6. Light/Dark + responsive — controls legible in both themes; desktop + 375px; no console errors.

Acceptance: filter UI updated + applies live; per-image persistence via computed(); included in payload; light + dark; no any; no console errors.
